POLICY-PROPERTY-FIRE-01::Coverage.text:
Fire coverage pays for direct physical loss to the insured dwelling and
attached structures caused by fire or smoke, including firefighting
efforts (e.g. water damage from extinguishing the fire). Coverage extends
to detached structures (garages, sheds) at 10% of the dwelling coverage
limit, and to personal property inside the dwelling at 50% of the dwelling
coverage limit.

Additional Living Expenses (ALE) are covered up to 20% of the dwelling
limit if the dwelling is rendered uninhabitable by a covered fire.

POLICY-PROPERTY-FIRE-01::Exclusions.text:
Fire coverage does NOT apply to:
- Fire caused intentionally by the policyholder or at the policyholder's
  direction.
- Loss where the dwelling had been vacant for more than 60 consecutive
  days prior to the fire, unless a vacancy permit was on file.
- Damage from a fire that started on a neighboring property and is
  primarily the neighboring property owner's liability (subrogation
  applies).
- Loss to property specifically excluded under a scheduled personal
  property endorsement (fine art, jewelry above stated limits).

POLICY-PROPERTY-FIRE-01::Deductible & Li.text:
- Standard deductible: 1% of dwelling coverage limit or $1,000, whichever
  is greater.
- Dwelling coverage limit: as stated on the policy declarations page, up to
  $500,000 under this policy tier.

POLICY-PROPERTY-FIRE-01::Claim Filing Re.text:
Claims must be reported within 5 days of the fire. A fire department
incident report is required for any claim exceeding $5,000. Claims lacking
a fire department report and exceeding this threshold are routed to
manual review before payout.

POLICY-AUTO-COLLISION-01::Coverage.text:
Collision coverage pays for damage to the policyholder's own vehicle
resulting from a collision with another vehicle or object, or from the
vehicle overturning, regardless of fault. This includes single-vehicle
accidents (e.g. striking a guardrail, pothole, or parked car).

Covered losses are paid up to the vehicle's actual cash value (ACV) at the
time of loss, less the applicable deductible.

POLICY-AUTO-COLLISION-01::Exclusions.text:
Collision coverage does NOT apply to:
- Damage from normal wear and tear, mechanical breakdown, or road debris
  that does not involve a collision (see Comprehensive Coverage).
- Damage sustained while the vehicle was being used for commercial
  ride-sharing or delivery purposes, unless a commercial-use rider is on
  file.
- Damage sustained while the vehicle was being operated by a driver not
  listed on the policy, unless that driver had reasonable belief they were
  entitled to operate the vehicle.
- Racing, speed contests, or off-road use.
- Intentional damage caused by the policyholder.

POLICY-AUTO-COLLISION-01::Deductible & L.text:
- Standard deductible: $500 per incident (policyholder may elect $250 or
  $1,000 at binding).
- Coverage limit: actual cash value of the vehicle at time of loss, up to
  $75,000.

POLICY-AUTO-COLLISION-01::Claim Filing R.text:
Claims must be reported within 30 days of the incident date. A police
report is required for any collision involving another vehicle, a
pedestrian, or damage exceeding $2,000. Claims reported more than 60 days
after the incident date are subject to additional review before payout.

POLICY-PROPERTY-WATER-01::Coverage.text:
Water damage coverage pays for sudden and accidental water discharge from
plumbing, heating, air conditioning, or household appliances (e.g. a burst
pipe or failed water heater), including the cost of tearing out and
replacing the portion of the dwelling necessary to access and repair the
source. Coverage extends to resulting damage to personal property at 50%
of the dwelling coverage limit.

POLICY-PROPERTY-WATER-01::Exclusions.text:
Water damage coverage does NOT apply to:
- Flood, meaning surface water, overflow of a body of water, or
  storm-driven surge (this requires separate flood insurance, typically
  through NFIP).
- Gradual leakage occurring over a period of more than 14 days, or damage
  the policyholder knew about and failed to remediate.
- Sewer or drain backup, unless the Sewer Backup Endorsement is on file.
- Water damage resulting from the policyholder's failure to maintain
  reasonable heat in the dwelling during freezing conditions, if the
  dwelling was left unoccupied.
- Mold remediation beyond $5,000, unless directly and immediately resulting
  from an otherwise-covered water discharge.

POLICY-PROPERTY-WATER-01::Deductible & L.text:
- Standard deductible: $1,000 per incident.
- Dwelling coverage limit: as stated on the policy declarations page, up to
  $500,000 under this policy tier.

POLICY-PROPERTY-WATER-01::Claim Filing R.text:
Claims must be reported within 5 days of discovering the damage. The
policyholder must take reasonable steps to prevent further damage (e.g.
shutting off the water supply) once the source is discovered; failure to
do so may reduce the payable amount. Photos of the source of the leak are
required.

POLICY-PROPERTY-THEFT-01::Coverage.text:
Theft coverage pays for personal property stolen from the insured dwelling
or, at reduced limits, from a vehicle or while traveling ("off-premises"
theft, covered at 10% of the personal property limit). Coverage includes
damage to the dwelling caused by forced entry during a burglary (broken
door, window).

POLICY-PROPERTY-THEFT-01::Exclusions.text:
Theft coverage does NOT apply to:
- Theft by a resident of the household or a person regularly employed on
  the premises (e.g. a live-in caretaker), except as provided by law.
- Loss of cash, unless specifically scheduled, beyond $200.
- Jewelry, watches, and furs beyond $1,500 combined, unless separately
  scheduled on a Valuable Items Endorsement.
- Theft from a dwelling under construction or vacant for more than 60
  consecutive days.
- Business property beyond $2,500, unless a home-business endorsement is on
  file.

POLICY-PROPERTY-THEFT-01::Deductible & L.text:
- Standard deductible: $500 per incident.
- Personal property coverage limit: 50% of dwelling coverage limit, up to
  $250,000.

POLICY-PROPERTY-THEFT-01::Claim Filing R.text:
A police report is REQUIRED for all theft claims and must be filed within
48 hours of discovery. An itemized list of stolen property with
approximate purchase dates and values must be submitted; claims lacking
this itemization are routed to manual review.

POLICY-AUTO-THEFT-01::Coverage.text:
Theft coverage (part of Comprehensive Coverage) pays for the loss of the
policyholder's vehicle due to theft, and for damage caused by attempted
theft (e.g. broken window, forced ignition damage, stripped catalytic
converter). Personal belongings left inside the vehicle are NOT covered
under this policy — see the policyholder's homeowners/renters policy for
personal property coverage.

If the vehicle is recovered within 30 days of the theft report, the claim
converts to a damage claim for repairs rather than a total-loss payout.

POLICY-AUTO-THEFT-01::Exclusions.text:
Theft coverage does NOT apply to:
- Theft by a resident of the policyholder's household or a person listed
  as an authorized driver on the policy.
- Loss where the keys were left in the ignition or the vehicle was left
  running and unattended in a non-secured location.
- Theft occurring more than 30 days after the policy lapsed for
  non-payment.
- Mysterious disappearance without evidence of forced entry or a police
  report.

POLICY-AUTO-THEFT-01::Deductible & Limit.text:
- Standard deductible: $500 per incident.
- Coverage limit: actual cash value of the vehicle at time of loss, up to
  $75,000. Aftermarket equipment (stereo systems, custom rims) is covered
  only up to $1,000 combined unless separately scheduled.

POLICY-AUTO-THEFT-01::Claim Filing Requi.text:
A police report is REQUIRED for all theft claims and must be filed within
48 hours of discovery. Claims without an accompanying police report number
will not be processed and are routed to manual review. The claimed vehicle
value must be supported by registration and, where available, maintenance
records.

POLICY-AUTO-COMPREHENSIVE-01::Coverage.text:
Comprehensive coverage pays for damage to the policyholder's vehicle from
causes other than collision, including: fire, falling objects, hail,
flooding, windstorm, vandalism, and contact with an animal (e.g. hitting a
deer). It also covers glass damage (windshield chips/cracks) and, as
described in the Auto Theft Coverage document, theft and attempted theft.

POLICY-AUTO-COMPREHENSIVE-01::Exclusions.text:
Comprehensive coverage does NOT apply to:
- Mechanical or electrical breakdown unrelated to a covered peril.
- Damage from freezing, unless caused by a covered weather event.
- Wear, tear, and gradual deterioration (tire wear, rust, corrosion).
- Loss occurring while the vehicle is used for commercial purposes without
  a commercial-use rider.
- Confiscation or destruction by government or civil authority.

POLICY-AUTO-COMPREHENSIVE-01::Deductible.text:
- Standard deductible: $250 per incident (glass-only claims may qualify for
  a $0 deductible under the Glass Endorsement, if elected).
- Coverage limit: actual cash value of the vehicle at time of loss, up to
  $75,000.

POLICY-AUTO-COMPREHENSIVE-01::Claim Fili.text:
Claims must be reported within 30 days of discovering the damage. Weather
-related claims (hail, flooding, windstorm) should reference the
corresponding date and location of the weather event where possible, as
this may be cross-checked against public weather records during review.

POLICY-OTHER-01::Coverage.text:
This document covers claim types that do not fall cleanly under Auto
Collision, Auto Theft, Auto Comprehensive, Property Fire, Property Water,
Property Theft, or Liability coverage — for example, claims involving
multiple coverage types, claims describing an ambiguous or unusual loss,
or claims where the loss type stated by the claimant does not match the
policy's defined coverage categories.

Such claims are not automatically denied. They should be evaluated against
the closest matching coverage type(s) above, and where coverage is
genuinely unclear, routed to a human reviewer rather than auto-adjudicated.

POLICY-OTHER-01::Exclusions.text:
- Losses with no identifiable covered peril (e.g. general deterioration,
  unexplained loss with no supporting detail).
- Claims for coverage types not written under this policy at all (e.g. a
  flood claim when only fire/water-discharge coverage, not NFIP flood
  insurance, is in force).

POLICY-OTHER-01::Deductible & Limits.text:
Not applicable at the document level — refer to the deductible and limit of
whichever specific coverage type the claim is ultimately matched to.

POLICY-OTHER-01::Claim Filing Requiremen.text:
Claims that cannot be confidently matched to a single coverage type within
this document set should be flagged with `is_covered = None` (inconclusive)
by the Policy Retrieval Agent rather than guessed, and escalated for human
review under the "ambiguous policy coverage" reason.

POLICY-LIABILITY-01::Coverage.text:
Liability coverage pays on behalf of the policyholder for bodily injury or
property damage to third parties for which the policyholder is legally
responsible, arising out of an auto accident or a covered premises
incident. This includes the cost of the third party's medical expenses,
property repair, and, where applicable, the policyholder's legal defense
costs, up to the policy limit.

POLICY-LIABILITY-01::Exclusions.text:
Liability coverage does NOT apply to:
- Injury or damage the policyholder intended to cause.
- Liability arising from the policyholder's business or professional
  activities, unless a business liability rider is on file.
- Contractual liability assumed by the policyholder beyond what would exist
  at law in the absence of the contract.
- Liability to a co-insured under the same policy (e.g. one household
  member suing another).
- Damage to property owned by, rented to, or in the care of the
  policyholder.

POLICY-LIABILITY-01::Deductible & Limits.text:
- No deductible applies to liability payouts to third parties.
- Per-occurrence limit: $100,000 bodily injury / $50,000 property damage
  under this policy tier, unless a higher-limit endorsement is on file.

POLICY-LIABILITY-01::Claim Filing Requir.text:
Claims must be reported as soon as reasonably possible, and always within
14 days of the policyholder becoming aware of a potential claim (including
being notified of a lawsuit or demand letter). Any correspondence from the
third party or their attorney must be forwarded immediately; the
policyholder should not admit fault or negotiate directly.
